journey.name: Live heart rate on any strap, on iOS
journey.description: A heart-rate strap or armband of any make, Polar's too, pairs in Settings on an iPhone and shows the heart rate live in a workout and a Lift session over CoreBluetooth; none records a class on iOS. Needs a real iPhone with Bluetooth on and a strap charged and worn: the simulator has no Bluetooth (there, Pair only raises the prompt and then says Bluetooth is off), so this one is run by hand on a fresh install.

actions.action: Open the app; verify that no Bluetooth prompt shows at launch. On the welcome tap "Skip to Set up", then "Skip for now"
Tap the gear on "Today" and scroll to "Body and heart rate"; verify that the sensor's row reads "Pair a sensor"

With the strap worn, tap "Pair a sensor" and allow Bluetooth when iOS asks; verify that the row reads "Looking for it…", then the strap's name over "Paired. Its heart rate shows live in workouts and sessions."
Go back to "Today" and verify that beside the gear a dot beats with the heart rate within a few seconds, and that no card offers "Record class" on a day with BJJ planned
Start a workout from "Train", "Conditioning"; verify that the heart-rate card under the ring reads the heart rate and, tapped, draws a trace
Lock the phone for a minute, then unlock it and return to the app: verify that the number returns within half a minute, and that the trace shows the gap
End the workout and verify that its summary shows the heart rate's average and peak; start a free session from "Train", "Strength" and verify that its heart card reads the heart rate
With a second sensor worn beside the first, tap "Forget", then "Pair a sensor": verify that "Which sensor?" lists both, the nearer first
In the iPhone's Settings, turn Bluetooth off for Interval, come back and tap "Pair a sensor": verify the notice "Bluetooth is off, or the app may not use it."
